idea-plugin.name: Lattice
idea-plugin.description:
Lattice — In-App Database Manager for IntelliJ IDEA

A database client for IntelliJ IDEA. Connect to, explore, query, create, and modify your databases without leaving your editor.

Key Features:

  • Supported Databases: MySQL, HSQLDB and PostgreSQL with a compatible JDBC driver. Tested server releases include MySQL 5.5, 5.6, 5.7 and 8.4, and HSQLDB 2.2.9 through 2.7.4 (Embedded File, In-Memory, and Server modes). PostgreSQL supports schema browsing, SQL consoles, data editing, DDL and exports with Java 8 compatible pgJDBC drivers; use 42.7.3 or 42.2.27 for servers older than 9.1.
  • Reusable JDBC Drivers: Download a driver version once and reuse it across connections and IDE restarts, or select a local JAR. Driver discovery runs in the background, supports Maven project defaults, and validates cached JARs before reuse.
  • Database Explorer: Tree view of Catalogs/Databases, Schemas, Tables, Views, Columns (with data types, primary key, and auto-increment indicators).
  • Interactive Data Grid: Inline cell editing with early type checking, auto-generated key protection, periodic auto-refresh, add/delete rows, batch commit, revert, filter (WHERE clause), a Clear filter action, and pagination. Actions reflect selection, pending edits and busy states.
  • SQL Query Console: Execute queries with Ctrl+Enter, result tables, affected row counts, elapsed time, and query history.
  • Visual DDL Wizards: Create databases, design tables, alter tables (add, rename, modify definition, and drop columns), truncate tables, and rename tables.
  • Export: Export data directly to CSV, JSON, and SQL INSERTs, and export/view CREATE TABLE DDL.

Coming soon:

Support for H2 and other relational databases is planned. The roadmap also includes generating POJOs, DTOs and JavaBeans; SQL syntax highlighting and schema-aware inline suggestions, subject to platform feasibility; and table relationship graphs and dependency trees. These features are not available yet.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Download JDBC drivers once and reuse them across connections and IDE restarts, with background discovery and cached JAR validation.
  • Clear table filters, use actions that reflect selection and pending edits, and work with improved layouts and light/dark styling.
  • Receive signed release builds with verified signatures and formatted release notes.
